newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end up after tumble, bargain hunting.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end up after tumble, bargain hunting.

text.p: Thai stocks reversed steep losses late on Monday, having slid over three percent in the morning, and closed slightly up as bargain hunters bought blue chips in the afternoon session, traders said.
The SET Index moved into positive territory shortly before the close and ended up 3.00 points at 819.79. The SET 50 closed up 0.20 points to 61.20 in 4.55 billion baht trade.
"There was talk that some long term European funds were buying in the afternoon as well as brokers buying for their own portfolios," said Tanawat Pitchimkul at Seamico Securities.
"Some stronger investors now seem willing to stomach the risks," he said referring to the afternoon buying.
But sentiment remains fragile and the upside was limited, traders said. Foreign selling had pushed prices down.
"I was quite surprised to see it end in the green. I think the rally is short term and I understand that overall foreign selling pressure is still quite strong," Tanawat said.
Krung Thai Bank topped the active list gaining 2.25 baht to 51, Thai Farmers Bank ended up one to 125 after sinking to 116 earlier and Securities One ended up nine to 107.
